FORM.AppraisalAddendumText: -::- 10/16/2026 Comp 6 is added to evaluate whether the subject's larger solar system warrants an additional adjustment. It has owned solar with approximately 59 reported panels, compared with the subject's reported 58 panels. It is included despite being over one mile from the subject to provide this additional solar comparison. The appraiser previously inspected Comp 6. Its reported living area, garage count, and ADU characteristics are based on that inspection and are consistent with the appraiser's prior reporting, although they may differ from other sources or appraisers. Market-derived adjustments account for differences from the subject. The $10,000 solar adjustment reflects the appraiser's analysis of market sales, including the owned-solar comparisons provided by Comps 3 and 6. As with a swimming pool, installation cost does not necessarily equal contributory market value. The sales analyzed do not support increasing the adjustment based solely on the reported system cost. Solar Electric (O) identifies systems analyzed as owned, and Solar Electric (L) identifies leased systems. Ownership and financing arrangements are considered separately; financing alone does not establish that a system is leased. Leased systems are excluded from contributory value, while owned systems are analyzed based on market evidence rather than installation cost. The contract requires the seller to pay the subject's remaining solar balance at closing. The appraisal relies on the extraordinary assumption that this payment satisfies purchase financing and that the buyer receives ownership without a continuing lease or third-party ownership interest. Supporting solar documents have not been provided. Use of this extraordinary assumption might affect the assignment results. The cited Berkeley Lab research provides broader historical context but does not establish the contributory value of the subject's solar system in its local market. The adjustment reflects the comparable sales analyzed in this appraisal. The additional analysis does not change the appraiser's opinion of value of $1,515,000. ============================================================================================== Disaster and External Conditions The subject property is not located in the vicinity of any recent FEMA-designated disasters and has not been impacted by fires, floods, debris flows, or other hazards. No physical damage to the property has been observed, and there is no indication that these events have affected the property. Appraisal Scope and Limitations This appraisal report is prepared exclusively for the client and other identified intended users for use in a mortgage transaction. The purpose of the appraisal is to develop an opinion of the market value of the subject property as of the effective date, based on the appraiser's inspection, analysis, and application of accepted appraisal methods, in compliance with the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP). This appraisal is not a home inspection. The appraiser's observations are limited to readily observable conditions at the time of inspection and are not intended to identify hidden, latent, or non-observable defects. The appraiser does not perform invasive inspections, test mechanical or electrical systems, or evaluate long-term performance, code compliance, or environmental conditions. Any references to system functionality are based solely on visual observation and typical market expectations unless otherwise noted. The appraisal is developed for valuation purposes only. No warranty or guarantee is made regarding the condition, safety, habitability, or future performance of the property or its components. Inspection reports, certifications, or evaluations prepared by third parties are outside the scope of this appraisal unless specifically referenced and relied upon. Heat Source Observation The heat source for the subject property is typical for the area, permanently installed, appears adequately sized for the dwelling, and is externally vented, based on the appraiser's general observation at the time of the inspection. The appraiser is not a heating specialist and does not perform detailed inspections or testing of the heating system's functionality, efficiency, or compliance with codes. For any concerns regarding the condition, performance, or suitability of the heat source, a licensed HVAC contractor should be consulted for a comprehensive evaluation. Smoke Alarm/CO Alarm Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors were observed to be present and showed no readily apparent physical damage at the time of inspection. The appraiser is not qualified to determine or certify their operational effectiveness under actual emergency conditions. No representation is made regarding functionality, sensitivity, remaining service life, or code compliance. Items such as ceiling fans, cabinetry, hardware, lighting fixtures, window coverings, and similar built-in or decorative features are typical for the market area and are generally reflected in the overall condition and quality ratings. These items are not adjusted for individually, as they do not contribute a measurable difference in market value when considered separately. External The subject and comparable properties are located within a similar residential setting with typical access to neighborhood services such as schools, retail, and transportation. These factors are common to the competitive market area and do not result in a measurable difference in value or marketability. No evidence of oil or gas activity is observed on the subject site. The subject and comparable properties are not influenced by golf course proximity. All comparable properties are located within the same competitive market area. Differences such as crossing major streets or minor physical boundaries were considered; however, market data does not indicate a consistent impact on value, and no location adjustment is applied. Properties reflect similar access, school influence, and overall neighborhood appeal. SUBJECT The subject property includes common utility easements, such as those for electrical, telephone, or water systems, which are typical in the market area. These easements match those found in comparable properties and, based on the appraiser's inspection, show no negative impact on the property's value, marketability, or use. ANSI Finished square footage based on the ANSI Measurement Standard 2021 and derived from approximate onsite measurements which are taken in tenths of a foot and rounded to the nearest whole foot. See attached photos and sketch page for dimensions and details. All measurements are for above grade spaces. Market Conditions Market conditions are analyzed using TrueTracts data for competitive properties within the subject's market area, with an effective date of 10/8/2026. The analysis includes 34 closed sales over the past 12 months and 3 pending/contingent listings. After accounting for property feature differences, the modeled average sale price decreases from $1,220,700 to $1,216,500, a change of approximately ?0.3%, supporting a relatively stable price trend. Housing supply increases from 4.5 to 6.0 months and is classified as oversupplied. Average days on market increases from 51 to 54 days. Sale prices average 97.3% of final list prices and 95.0% of original list prices. Distressed sales represent approximately 3.4% of sales. Seller concessions occur in approximately 55.0% of sales, averaging 1.1% of the sale price among transactions with concessions. Time adjustments are derived from the TrueTracts Generalized Additive Model, which accounts for property feature differences and measures price movement since each comparables contract date through the most recent monthly period available as of the appraisal's effective date. The adjustments are small, consistent with the limited movement measured during the applicable periods, and are applied to reflect those changes in accordance with Fannie Mae guidelines. The relatively stable overall price trend does not preclude adjustments for movement during individual comparable contract periods. Highest & Best Use Legally Permissible The subject is improved with a single-family residence and appears to comply with current zoning requirements. Physically Possible The subject improvements, including the dwelling, garage, and patios, are appropriate for the site and do not appear to exceed zoning limitations. Based on typical development patterns in the area, the site appears capable of supporting the existing improvements. If destroyed, reconstruction of a similar single-family dwelling would generally be permissible subject to local building requirements. Financially Feasible Market evidence indicates that residential development of similar single-family dwellings in the area is economically viable. Construction of a similar dwelling would typically be supported by market value relative to development costs. Maximally Productive Given zoning restrictions and surrounding development patterns, the most productive use of the site as improved is its current use as a single-family residence. No alternative use appears legally permissible or economically supported. GEOGRAPHIC COMPETENCY The appraiser has been appraising properties within the subject's market area since 2002 and is familiar with the characteristics of the local market and the subject property type. The appraiser has prior experience analyzing and appraising similar properties and possesses the competency necessary to complete this assignment in conformity with the Competency Rule of USPAP. SPECIAL ASSESSMENTS Public records reflect routine tax components and bond charges that are collected through the annual property tax bill and are typical for properties in the area. These items are considered part of the overall tax rate and do not represent reportable special assessments. Based on the information available to the appraiser, no energy-related financing obligations (such as PACE or HERO) are known to exist. If such obligations are later identified, they may warrant further review, as they can affect marketability and value. PREDOMINANT VALUE The subject property is consistent with the predominant property type in the neighborhood, which consists primarily of single-family residential dwellings similar in age, design, and utility. Based on market data summarized in the 1004MC and supported by comparable sales in this report, the concluded value of the subject falls within the typical value range for the neighborhood and does not represent an over-improvement or under-improvement relative to surrounding properties. Neighborhood/Market Search Parameters The search parameters applied in selecting comparable properties are intended to filter out non-similar sales while focusing on properties that reflect competitive alternatives to the subject. In some cases, the search area may extend beyond a typical one-mile radius; however, the identified markets are generally compatible in terms of buyer appeal, price range, and housing characteristics. The selected comparables are considered reasonable substitutes and appropriate indicators of market behavior for the subject property. My Comparable Search & Results Feature Filter Bathrooms 2.5-5 Bedrooms 3-5 Garage spaces 2-6 Living area 3,040-5,070 sf Site size 51,000-153,000 sf Year built 1970-2025 Sale price $937,000-$1,809,000 The sale-price filter is used only to remove extreme price outliers. The model uses 5 years of competing sales within the defined subject submarket. Comparable search uses a 12 month look-back time frame. The appraiser considered various sales that were larger, smaller, inferior, and superior during the appraisal process. These sales were evaluated as part of the overall market analysis to identify properties that are competitive with the subject. The comparable sales selected for inclusion in the grid represent the most similar properties in terms of location, site size, gross living area, condition, and overall utility. Other sales and listings, both at lower and higher price points, were also considered as part of the analysis to understand the broader market and support the final value conclusion. The selected comparables are considered the most appropriate and reliable indicators of value for the subject property, and the final opinion of value is based on their analyzed and adjusted sale prices. Concessions Concessions are common within the market and typically range from approximately 1% to 3% of the sale price. Adjustments are applied when verified concessions are determined to have influenced the reported sale price. The appraiser notes that concessions reported in the appraisal grid may differ from MLS-reported figures, as MLS systems may include agent commissions within concession fields. Agent commissions are not considered seller concessions for appraisal analysis purposes. Adjustment Methodology Adjustments in this report are developed through a data-supported analysis of comparable sales within the subject's competitive market area. Methods considered include Generalized Additive Modeling, peer adjustment data, depreciated cost, paired sales/sensitivity analysis, and review of the comparable sales used in the report. These methods are used to identify the market's reaction to differences in individual property features. Final adjustments are reconciled by the appraiser based on the most applicable indicators, the quality of the available data, and the overall comparability of each sale. The TrueTracts adjustment analysis supports this methodology and includes GAM, Peer Adjustments, Depreciated Cost, and Sensitivity Analysis as separate indicators for feature-level adjustments. Condition Analysis Condition ratings are based on available information, including MLS descriptions, photos, agent comments, and exterior observations of the comparable sales. Interior inspections of the comparable sales were not performed. Each comparable is evaluated using the standard UAD condition rating system. Condition adjustments reflect market reaction to differences in updating, maintenance, and overall condition as indicated by the available data. Adjustments and Rationale GLA: Adjusted at $141.00 per sqft Reflects market reaction to differences in living area. The adjustment is supported by statistical modeling, peer adjustment data, and review of the comparable sales, with consideration given to diminishing returns and the degree of difference between the subject and each comparable. Site: Site size differences are adjusted at $2.00 per square foot for sites smaller than the subject. For sites larger than the subject, the adjustment rate is reduced to $0.50 per square foot, or 25% of the base rate, to reflect diminishing contributory value as site size increases. Adjustments reflect market reaction to differences in site size and utility. Bedrooms: Adjusted at $5,000 per bedroom Reflects differences in functional utility and market preference for bedroom count. The adjustment is applied when the difference is considered meaningful to buyers and supported by the available data. Bathrooms: Adjusted at $12,000 per full / $6,000 per half Reflects differences in bathroom count and functional utility. The adjustment is based on the contributory value indicated by market data and the overall layout of the comparable property. Garage Spaces: Adjusted at $10,000 per space Reflects market reaction to covered parking and storage utility. The adjustment is supported by statistical modeling, peer adjustment data, depreciated cost, and review of the comparable sales where applicable. Stories: Adjusted at $7,000 Reflects market reaction to single-story versus multi-story design, when supported by the available comparable data. Pool: Adjusted at $60,000 Reflects the market-supported contributory value of pool amenities within the subject's competitive market area. AGE Age adjustments were not applied, as the subject and comparable properties are of similar overall vintage and the market does not demonstrate a consistent value reaction to minor differences in chronological age. Differences in depreciation, updates, or modernization are reflected through condition ratings and supported by the comparable sales used in this report. Fireplace: Adjustments are based on market evidence from the sales used in the grid. A "0" indicates no impact. Porches/Patios Differences in covered porches, covered patios, enclosed patios, and slab patios were considered. Based on the available market data, the contributory value of these individual features could not be reliably isolated; therefore, no separate adjustments were applied despite differences among the subject and comparable properties. The appraiser has adjusted dissimilarities between the subject and comparables according to market reaction. A "0" adjustment indicates the difference was analyzed; however, the market does not demonstrate a measurable reaction warranting an adjustment. SUBJECT GLA The subject property was measured to be 51sf smaller than indicated in public records, with no impact on its value. All sides were measured and are square. For the purposes of this appraisal, the measured living area is utilized, which is for the sole use of the client and its assignees in making a lending decision. The reported gross living area (GLA) of comparable sales is based on information from MLS and public records. The appraiser did not measure the comparable properties, and ANSI compliance of comparables cannot be verified. This information is considered reliable and is standard industry practice for appraisal purposes COMPARABLE ANALYSIS Comparable sales were initially identified through the local MLS. Verification of sales price, buyer, seller, and recording information was obtained through public records (Realist/assessor's data), which is considered a reliable independent source. MLS was relied upon for supplemental information such as listing history, property condition comments, and marketing details. The sale dates referenced in this report reflect the contract date (date the property went under contract), not the close of escrow date. For reporting and time-adjustment purposes, sales are categorized based on their contract date relative to the effective date. Comp 1 went under contract within the 6 months prior to the effective date. Comps 2 & 3 went under contract more than 6 months prior to the effective date. Inclusion of these sales was necessary due to limited availability of more recent competitive data. Comps 4 and 5 are located over one mile away from the subject property and are included due to the lack of comparable listings closer to the subject. Comps 1-3 are closed sales located within 0.09-0.61 miles of the subject and provide comparisons across living area, site size, and amenities, with similar age, Q3 quality, C3 condition, and pool/spa features. Comp 1 is a recent one-story sale with smaller living area and site size, an additional full bathroom and garage space, and a reported casita. Comp 2 has similar living area, bedroom and bathroom counts, and garage capacity, while its larger site brackets the subject's site size. Comp 3 is on the same street as the subject and provides a larger living-area comparison, with a smaller site and an additional bedroom. Its reported 7 garage spaces are based on MLS data; MLS photos show an RV-type garage. The garage adjustment reflects contributory utility and is consistent with the paired-sales analysis used for garage differences. Comps 4 and 5 are a pending listing and an active listing located 1.03 and 1.19 miles from the subject, respectively, and are included to evaluate current competition and market trends. Both have similar Q3 quality and C3 condition ratings. Comp 4 has a similar site size, smaller living area, additional bedrooms and a full bathroom, and dirt-road access. Comp 5 has similar living area, a smaller site, one-story design, an additional garage space, no pool, and one fewer half bathroom. RECONCILIATION The closed sales range from $1,395,000 to $1,565,000 before adjustments and from $1,487,700 to $1,519,100 after adjustments. Most weight is given to Comp 3, located on the subject's street approximately 0.09 miles away, due to its similar age, design, quality, condition, and pool/spa amenities. Although its contract date is more than 12 months before the effective date, a time adjustment accounts for the measured market movement during that period. Comps 1 and 2 provide support and receive secondary consideration. The pending and active listings provide additional context regarding current competition. The appraiser concludes a market value of $1,515,000, which is $135,000 below the $1,650,000 contract price. Within the noted search parameters?sales during the prior 12 months within 2 miles and with living area within approximately 1,000 square feet of the subject?only 1 sale exceeds $1,600,000, at approximately $1,800,000. That sale is a newer home with differences in construction age and site improvements that limit its comparability. Other sales reviewed outside these parameters are addressed separately. The selected sales and current competition do not support the subject's contract price. Personal property is not given value or consideration in the opinion of value. Considered Not Used 17289 Mariposa Avenue, Riverside, CA 92504 (MLS OC25215520), sold for $1,725,000 on January 5, 2026, and is reviewed for additional market context but not selected as a comparable sale. MLS reports 2,836 square feet of living area, 4 bedrooms, 3 full bathrooms, and a combined site area of 96,703 square feet (2.22 acres) across 2 parcels. The dwelling is substantially smaller than the subject's 4,054 square feet and falls outside the noted living-area search parameters. It is reviewed to examine higher-priced transactions in the surrounding market. Improvements include an approximately 2,400-square-foot workshop with a bathroom and vehicle lifts, an attached 3-car garage, a detached 2-car garage, and extensive pool/spa and outdoor cooking amenities. The combination of these improvements introduces substantial differences in utility from the subject and limits its usefulness as a direct comparison. 15421 Shelton Drive, Perris, CA 92570 (MLS OC26106910), sold for $1,675,000, and 20390 Christo Court, Lake Mathews, CA 92570 (MLS IG26057974), sold for $1,650,000. Both sales are reviewed during an expanded 3-mile search but are not selected as comparable properties. Both have superior lake views relative to the subject and are located over two miles away. These differences limit their comparability, and the selected sales provide more similar comparisons. Appraiser Additional Certifications ? USPAP Identification: Comments on Appraisal and Report Identification I performed this appraisal in accordance with the requirements of the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice that were adopted and promulgated by the Appraisal Standards Board of The Foundation and that were in place at the time this appraisal report was prepared. The Appraiser certifies and agrees that: (1) The analyses, opinions and conclusions were developed, and this report was prepared, in conformity with the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice ("USPAP"), and in accordance with the regulations developed by the Lender's Federal Regulatory Agency as required by FIRREA. (2) Compensation is not contingent upon the reporting of predetermined value or direction that favors the cause of the client, the amount of the value estimate, the attainment of a stipulated result, or the occurrence of a subsequent event. (3) This appraisal assignment was not based on a requested minimum valuation, a specific valuation, or the approval of a loan. The Sales Comparison Approach was given the most weight in the final value conclusion for the subject property, as it demonstrates the Principle of Substitution and best reflects the attitudes of typically informed buyers and sellers in this market area. This appraisal is based on the information made available to the appraiser as of the effective date. Should additional material information or revised assignment conditions be provided after completion of the appraisal, additional analysis or report revisions may be required. Income Approach Not Developed The income approach was considered but not developed for this assignment. Market participants in this property type and market area typically rely on owner-occupant purchasing decisions rather than income-producing potential when establishing value. In addition, sufficient market data necessary to develop a reliable Gross Rent Multiplier (GRM) or income capitalization analysis was not available or considered adequately comparable. The Cost Approach was developed. However, due to the lack of recent, relevant land sales and the difficulty in measuring accrued depreciation, the Cost Approach is considered to be less reliable. The Cost Approach is NOT intended to be used for insurance purposes. The Intended User of this appraisal report is the Lender/Client. Unless specifically stated within the report, there are no additional Intended Users. The Intended Use is to evaluate the property that is the subject of this appraisal for a mortgage finance transaction, subject to the stated Scope of Work, purpose of the appraisal, reporting requirements of this appraisal report form, and Definition of Market Value, as defined within the report. The Market Value concluded in this appraisal report was prepared for federally related mortgage loan purposes and is in conformance with the requirements of Title XI of the Federal Financial Institutions Reform, Recovery and Enforcement Act of 1989 (FIRREA), the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP), the Secondary Market and Valuation Support Services. The final value concluded in this appraisal analysis is current, as of the effective date of the appraisal. Assumptions and Limiting Conditions: This appraisal is based on the assumption that information obtained from public records, MLS, third-party sources, and parties with an interest in the transaction is accurate unless otherwise noted. The appraiser did not perform structural, mechanical, environmental, or code compliance inspections and is not qualified to render opinions in those disciplines. No representation is made regarding the condition, performance, or remaining life of structural components, mechanical systems, utilities, or environmental conditions beyond what was readily observable at the time of inspection. Any latent defects, code violations, or conditions not visible during a normal appraisal inspection are outside the scope of this appraisal. If additional information becomes available, the appraiser reserves the right to revise the analysis and conclusions. This appraisal report is not intended to be utilized as a property inspection. The visual inspection performed by this appraiser is limited in nature, as the appraiser is not an expert in the field of property inspection. Should the intended user of this appraisal report have concerns regarding the subject property, the intended user is urged to consult with a professional property inspector. The appraiser made a personal inspection of the subject property (both interior and exterior) and a personal exterior inspection from the street of all comparable sales and listings used in the report. APPRAISER INDEPENDENCE No employee, director, officer, or agent of the Seller, or any other third party acting as joint venture partner, independent contractor, appraisal company, appraisal management company, or partner on behalf of the Seller has influenced or attempted to influence the development, reporting, result, or review of this assignment through coercion, extortion, collusion, compensation, instruction, inducement, intimidation, bribery or in any other manner. I represent and warrant that, as of the date of this Report, I have had no contact with anyone that would in any way be construed as a violation of the Appraiser Independence Requirements; the only individuals with whom I have had any contact regarding my preparation of this Report have been limited to representatives of the appraisal management company and the designated individual required for entry into the subject property for purposes of inspection. No agent or representative of lender/client whose name appears on the first page of this Report has contacted me directly and I am obligated to and would report any such unauthorized contact, whether in person, by phone, or electronically, to the appraisal management company immediately.
